content.value_statement: Teams lose useful lessons when task reflections stay isolated. This skill aggregates repeated patterns into a compact record for future improvement.
actual_capabilities: Defines a local aggregate file for cross-task reflection summaries.
Specifies how to update strategy effectiveness from new reflections.
Tracks repeated failures, bottlenecks, discoveries, and proposals.
Provides similarity matching rules for merging related patterns.
Defines thresholds for best practices, anti-patterns, and skill candidates.
Shows query patterns for prioritizing improvements from aggregate data.
limitations: Requires existing reflection files with consistent fields.
Does not provide executable scripts or automated validation.
Uses fuzzy matching guidance that depends on reviewer judgment.
Stores only local aggregate learning and does not sync across systems.

use_cases.title: Improve Repeated Workflows
use_cases.description: Aggregate recent task reflections to find strategies that consistently help or fail.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Skill Evolution
use_cases.description: Use repeated proposals and failure patterns to choose the next skill improvement.

use_cases.title: Build Shared Learning Memory
use_cases.description: Turn isolated task notes into trend data that supports future Claude, Codex, and Claude Code work.

prompt_templates.title: Create First Aggregate
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup after several task reflections exist.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the recent task reflections and create the first cross-task aggregate. Include task count, common strategies, failures, and proposals.

prompt_templates.title: Update After Reflection
prompt_templates.scenario: Routine update after one completed task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the cross-task aggregate using the latest reflection. Merge similar patterns, update counts, and keep the newest task history entries.

prompt_templates.title: Find Improvement Priorities
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the aggregate and list the top improvement priorities. Rank active failures, repeated proposals, and ready skill candidates.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Learning Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the aggregate for duplicate patterns, stale entries, weak evidence, and threshold errors. Recommend precise cleanup actions.

output_examples.input: Several reflections mention parallel exploration as successful and contract conflicts as recurring failures.
output_examples.output: The aggregate highlights parallel exploration as a strong practice and marks contract conflicts as a high-priority active failure.

output_examples.input: A recurring discovery appears in three task reflections but is not documented elsewhere.
output_examples.output: The aggregate marks the discovery for documentation and raises it as a knowledge-base candidate.

output_examples.input: Five reflections propose the same implementation-cycle workflow as a reusable pattern.
output_examples.output: The aggregate marks the workflow as a skill candidate because it meets the frequency threshold.

best_practices: Update the aggregate immediately after each individual reflection.
Merge similar patterns using clear evidence before increasing counts.
Keep aggregate entries compact and focused on repeated signals.
anti_patterns: Do not copy full reflections into the aggregate file.
Do not treat one task as proof of a broad pattern.
Do not ignore stale failures after related fixes are completed.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It defines a local aggregate record for repeated lessons from task reflections.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and update guidance for local reflection data.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that maintain reflection files.

faq.question: What data should be included?
faq.answer: Include repeated strategies, failures, bottlenecks, discoveries, proposals, and task outcomes.

faq.question: How are similar patterns merged?
faq.answer: The skill recommends normalization, word overlap, and shared key terms.

faq.question: Can it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. It organizes evidence, but reviewers should verify patterns before acting.
